description.narrative:
JASS har ansökt till Sida om finansiering på 40 miljoner SEK som kärnstöd till deras strategiska plan under 2020 till 2024.
Interventionen syftar till att bygga och stärka kvinnorörelser, dvs. att utrusta och stödja kvinnor, aktivister och organisationer att organisera sig och stärka sin kapacitet att bidra till samhällsförändring och utmana ojämlikhet, diskriminering, våld och miljöförstöring. De konkreta aktiviteterna inkluderar;
1) Feministiska ledarskapsskolor och cirklar med utbildningsprogram som genomförs på lokal, regional och global nivå och som kombinerar möten IRL med virtuella möten. Utbildningsprogrammen finns på plats i Honduras, Guatemala, Mexiko, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Kambodja, Indonesien, Myanmar och Filippinerna. De täcker bland annat feministisk ekonomisk läskunnighet, proaktiva kommunikationsstrategier, personlig säkerhet. Inriktning och innehåll baseras alltid på vad som är relevant och efterfrågat i varje land.
2) Mentorskap/ följeslagarverksamhet för att bygga och stärka rörelser och bidra till att stödja kvinnor och deras organisationer när de tar på sig an politiskt svåra frågor. Denna typ av stöd till kvinnor och deras organisationer gör det möjligt för JASS att stärka lokala partners organisatoriska förmåga att reagera på brådskande situationer som sätter säkerhet och försörjning för aktivister och kvinnliga människorättsförsvarare i fara.
JASS kommer att genomföra interventionen genom sina regionkontor i Afrika, Latinamerika och Sydostasien samt med lokala partners.
Insatsens totala budget är cirka 34 miljoner USD för femårsperioden. JASS får kärnstöd bland annat från det nederländska utrikesministeriet, Novo Foundation, OAK Foundation och Open Society Foundation samt projektstöd från olika givare för specifika lands- eller regionala program.
Finansieringen från Sida kommer att utgöra cirka 12-15% av den årliga budgeten. Cirka 20% av den årliga budgeten kommer att vidarebefordras.

JASS has applied to Sida for funding of 40 million SEK as core support to their strategic plan during 2020 to 2024.
The intervention aims at movement building i.e. to equip and support grassroot women's activists and organizations to build and organize power and capacity to lead fundamental change policies, institutions and social norms to challenge inequality, discrimination, violence and environment destruction.
The concrete activities include; 1) Feminist leadership Schools and Circles with training programs that are carried out on local regional and global level and that combine face to face convenings with virtual meetings. Training programs are in place in Honduras, Guatemala, Mexico, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Cambodia, Indonesia, Myanmar and Philippines. They cover feminist economic literacy, proactive communication strategies, personal safety and more. The setup, content and length is always based on what's relevant and requested in each country.
2) Political Accompaniment to build and strengthen movements and helps sustain women and their organizations as they take on critical agendas and build power. This type of support to women and their organizations allows JASS to strengthen the organizational capacity of local partners to respond to urgent situations that place the safety and livelihood of activists and women human rights defenders at risk.
JASS will implement the intervention through their regional offices in Africa, Latin America and Southeast Asia and with local partners.
The intervention’s total budget is approximately 34 million USD for the 5 year period. JASS is getting core support also from the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Novo Foundation, OAK Foundation and Open Society Foundation as well as project support from various donors for specific country or regional programs.
The funding from Sida will constitute approximately 12-15% of the annual budget. Approximately 20% of the annual budget will be forwarded as sub-grants.

The overall objective of the intervention is: Strengthening womens activism, and cross-movement and cross-border networks for mutual protection and increased influence in the face of heightened political attacks against women on the frontlines.
The specific objectives are: 1. Bolster womens leadership and organizing capacity through scaled up training and political education, including offering newly systematized methodologies on applied power analysis, movement strategy, political narratives, collective activist safety and wellbeing, as well as fresh content on economic, environmental and political justice. Build on and promote JASS We Rise toolkit through schools and webinars. 2. Build and fortify cross-issue, cross-border movement alliances and links indigenous, environmental, feminist, human rights, LGBTI, workers, etc. within and across regions and in North-South exchanges for greater political leverage, strategic collaboration, and safety. 3. Influence thinking, policy, practice and funding within the international human rights and development community to better integrate gender, power and collective approaches to protection. 4. Center grassroots women's innovations and demands, and amplify grassroots feminist contributions from the Global South through advocacy and creative use of social media, JASS Women Crossing the Line platform and the production of knowledge (e.g. articles, research, blogs, curated discussions) to influence understanding of, and responses to, violence and inequality.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Result examples from the final report includes: (accumulated for the whole program period)
7433 activists participated in 328 Feminist Popular Education leadership workshops and schools across 22 countries. 80% of the participants reported increased confidence, knowledge, well-being and safety, as well as an increased ability to understand and articulate structural analysis of power.
In the report JASS describe how their support has contributed results in terms of women and non-binary persons gaining confidence and knowledge to engage in politics in Honduras, Guatemala and Mexico, to set up collective safety strategies for women environmental defenders in Honduras and to bring about changes in social norms related to gender based violence in Zimbabwe and Malawi.
JASS report how they have contributed to movement building for gender justice for instance through accompaniment to 70 partner organisations and conduction of 116 cross movement dialogues. They have in 2023 conducted a south to south exchange for 30 land and territory women and non-binary defenders. It is Sidas assessment that JASS is playing an important role by supporting local organizations and movements to cooperate and to articulate joint demands for the protection of their human rights as well as protection of their lands, health and against corruption.
JASS has during the program period contributed to making women's leadership more visible and has produced 330 publications that shared women's experiences, perspectives and solutions and have contributed to 500 instances of mainstream media coverage of Women Human Rights defenders agendas and demands.
JASS work has contributed to increased access and control over resources and improved implementation of laws and policies to eliminate discrimination and violence. Work in relation to this outcome is however difficult to measure. JASS report that they have contributed to activities engaging with 3 174 decision makers and 9 legal policy changes related to women's rights.
Impact examples on global level includes how JASS has contributed to the approval of the General Recommendation no. 39 on the Rights of Indigenous Women and Girls (CEDAW/C/GC/39) in October 2022 which was a significant step in recognizing discrimination and violence against Indigenous women and girls in Mesoamerica. JASS contributed through strategic planning, training and supporting advocacy campaigns with other civil society organisations, as well as through direct contributions to the submission of the draft text to CEDAW. Through this instrument, Indigenous women and girls have new opportunities to fight for their rights and to challenge discrimination, violence, poverty, and the lack of legal protection.
An example on impact on country level is the the ratification of the Sexual Violence Crime Bill in Indonesia in 2022, which is a law that addresses the rights of survivors of sexual violence. Under the new law, survivors of sexual violence now have the right to legal, mental, social and economic protection from the state, which is a direct addressing of demands of women's rights groups fighting against GBV and discrimination. The law has also increased public awareness of sexual violence, and avenues for reporting for survivors including knowledge of the governments sexual violence prevention and response programs. JASS reports that the collective advocacy for the ratification of the bill as law, was directly bolstered and inspired through JASS FPE workshops followed by cross movement alliance and agenda setting involving 5 local partners (FAMM, Rumah Kitab, Fahmina, Rahima, Perempuan Mahardika).
14 implementing partners in Malawi, South Africa, Honduras, Guatemala, Cambodia, Indonesia, Philpines and Thailand have received funding from Sidas grant.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
